Treatment effects on latent class membership within a subgroup

intervene_subgroup.Rd

\(\Delta_k(G) = P(C(1) = k \mid G) - P(C(0) = k \mid G)\) for a subgroup \(G\) defined by pre-treatment variables, by weighting the per-observation contributions of intervene_membership() (nuisance models fitted on the whole sample). Standard errors include the measurement model.

Usage

intervene_subgroup(
  model,
  data,
  treatment,
  confounders = NULL,
  subset,
  estimator = c("aipw", "ipw_bch"),
  propensity_model = "linear",
  outcome_model = "linear",
  folds = 5,
  trim = 0,
  seed = 1,
  learners = NULL,
  bound = 0.01
)

Arguments

model, data, treatment, confounders

As in intervene_membership() (data-frame interface).

subset

A logical condition evaluated in data (e.g. age < 30); NA counts as FALSE. It must not depend on the treatment or the indicators.

estimator

"aipw" (default) or "ipw_bch".

propensity_model, outcome_model

Working models for the propensity score (logistic regression) and the latent class regression: "linear" (main effects) or "quadratic" (adds squares, pairwise products and treatment-by-covariate terms). Machine-learning learners are also accepted (see learners).

folds

Number of cross-fitting folds (1 = no cross-fitting).

trim

Truncate estimated propensity scores to [trim, 1 - trim] (0 = no truncation).

seed

Random seed for the fold assignment.

learners

Machine-learning nuisance models. Besides "linear" and "quadratic", propensity_model and outcome_model accept a learner fitted within the cross-fitting training folds: "lasso", "lasso_quadratic", "elasticnet", "ridge" (penalised GLMs with cross-validated \(\lambda\)), "forest" (random forest), "boost" (gradient-boosted trees; needs the Julia package EvoTrees.jl) or "superlearner" (stacked ensemble). With a learner, the class regression estimates \(P(\hat c = j \mid A = a, X)\) in each arm and maps it through \(D^{-1}\). learners is the library of the "superlearner": a character vector of names ("mean", "glm", "glm_quadratic", "lasso", "lasso_quadratic", "elasticnet", "ridge", "forest", "boost"), or NULL for the default library (mean, glm, lasso, lasso_quadratic, forest).

bound

With a learner, propensity scores are bounded to [bound, 1 - bound] (forests can predict 0 or 1). Not applied to "linear" / "quadratic".

Value

An object of class c("lcc_subgroup_result", "lcc_result") (printed, tidied and plotted like intervene_membership() results; n is the subgroup size), with subgroup and n_total.

How to use

  1. Fit model and run intervene_membership() on the whole sample first.

  2. Write the subgroup as a condition on pre-treatment columns of data (subset = female == 1); NA counts as FALSE.

  3. Run intervene_subgroup(model, data, treatment, confounders, subset = ...); the nuisance models still use the whole sample.

  4. Repeat for the complementary subgroup and compare; no test of the difference between subgroups is reported. See vignette("function-guide").

See also

intervene_membership()

Examples

# \donttest{
data(programme)
# Question: is the programme's effect on the wellbeing classes similar for girls and boys?
m <- latentmixtures::lca(programme, low_mood:friends, K = 3)
#> Starting Julia ...
girls <- intervene_subgroup(m, programme, treatment = programme,
                            confounders = c(female, age, low_ses, distress, belonging),
                            subset = female == 1)
girls   # 1017 girls: Flourishing +0.163, Distressed -0.160
#>   Subgroup: female == 1 (1017 of 2000 analysed rows)
#> ▸ Causal effect of a treatment on latent class membership
#>   AIPW, BCH pseudo-outcomes, 5-fold cross-fitting; N = 1017, K = 3
#>   Treatment:    programme
#>   Confounders:  female, age, low_ses, distress, belonging
#> 
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>            P(C¹=k)  P(C⁰=k)       Δ     SE            95% CI      p
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   Class 1    0.580    0.420   0.160  0.044    [0.074, 0.246]  <.001
#>   Class 2    0.254    0.252   0.002  0.052   [−0.101, 0.104]   .975
#>   Class 3    0.166    0.328  −0.162  0.030  [−0.221, −0.102]  <.001
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#>   Δ = P(C¹=k) − P(C⁰=k); SE from the influence function incl. the measurement model.
#>   Diagnostics: entropy = 0.666, propensity range [0.022, 0.922]
boys <- intervene_subgroup(m, programme, treatment = programme,
                           confounders = c(female, age, low_ses, distress, belonging),
                           subset = female == 0)
boys    # 983 boys: Flourishing +0.231, Moderate -0.109, Distressed -0.121
#>   Subgroup: female == 0 (983 of 2000 analysed rows)
#> ▸ Causal effect of a treatment on latent class membership
#>   AIPW, BCH pseudo-outcomes, 5-fold cross-fitting; N = 983, K = 3
#>   Treatment:    programme
#>   Confounders:  female, age, low_ses, distress, belonging
#> 
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>            P(C¹=k)  P(C⁰=k)       Δ     SE            95% CI      p
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   Class 1    0.668    0.438   0.229  0.043    [0.144, 0.314]  <.001
#>   Class 2    0.230    0.336  −0.106  0.050  [−0.205, −0.008]   .035
#>   Class 3    0.103    0.225  −0.123  0.029  [−0.179, −0.066]  <.001
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#>   Δ = P(C¹=k) − P(C⁰=k); SE from the influence function incl. the measurement model.
#>   Diagnostics: entropy = 0.666, propensity range [0.022, 0.922]
# The intervals overlap and no test of the difference is reported: present both.
# }
